basics.description: **Note:** Please refer to the following before installing the solution: • Review the solution [Release Notes](https://github.com/Azure/Azure-Sentinel/tree/master/Solutions/HoneyForge/ReleaseNotes.md) • There may be [known issues](https://aka.ms/sentinelsolutionsknownissues) pertaining to this Solution, please refer to them before installing. The [HoneyForge](https://honeyforge.tech) solution for Microsoft Sentinel enables you to ingest HoneyForge honeypot deception sensor events into Microsoft Sentinel via CEF/AMA, providing visibility into attack sources, targeted sensors, protocols, and threat trends across your honeypot deployment. **Data Connectors:** 1, **Workbooks:** 1, **Analytic Rules:** 1, **Hunting Queries:** 5 [Learn more about Microsoft Sentinel](https://aka.ms/azuresentinel) | [Learn more about Solutions](https://aka.ms/azuresentinelsolutionsdoc)

options.text: This Solution installs the data connector for HoneyForge. You can get HoneyForge CommonSecurityLog data in your Microsoft Sentinel workspace. After installing the solution, configure and enable this data connector by following guidance in Manage solution view.

link.label: Learn more about connecting data sources

options.text: This solution installs workbook(s) to help you gain insights into the telemetry collected in Microsoft Sentinel. After installing the solution, start using the workbook in Manage solution view.
This solution installs the following analytic rule templates. After installing the solution, create and enable analytic rules in Manage solution view.

Detects an interaction with a HoneyForge deception sensor. Any activity
involving a HoneyForge sensor must be treated as potentially unauthorised
until validated by the security operations team.

HoneyForge sensors are passive decoy devices  - legitimate systems and users
should never communicate with them. Any detected interaction may indicate
network scanning, lateral movement, or an actively compromised device.
This solution installs the following hunting queries. After installing the solution, run these hunting queries to hunt for threats in Manage solution view.

elements.name: huntingquery1
elements.label: HoneyForge - Sensor Fleet Coverage and Health

options.text:
Provides a per-sensor event summary for the past 30 days, giving visibility
into which sensors are active, which are quiet, and which may be offline or
misconfigured (no events in the last 10 minutes is the offline threshold).

Use this query during routine operations to confirm full fleet coverage and
identify any gaps in your deception layer before an attacker does. This hunting query depends on HoneyForge data connector (CommonSecurityLog Parser or Table)

Detects source IPs generating an unusually high volume of events against
HoneyForge sensors in a short window (more than 50 events in any 10-minute
period). This pattern is characteristic of automated scanners, brute-force
tools, or worm-like lateral movement.

High-frequency hits deserve immediate triage  - especially if the source is
an internal IP, which would indicate a compromised or misconfigured device
inside the network. This hunting query depends on HoneyForge data connector (CommonSecurityLog Parser or Table)

Surfaces HoneyForge sensor interactions that occurred outside normal business
hours (before 07:00 or after 19:00 UTC, Monday to Friday, and all day on
weekends). Off-hours activity from internal IPs is especially suspicious  -
it may indicate a compromised device operating autonomously or an insider
threat.

Adjust the hour thresholds to match your organisation's working hours if
they differ from the defaults. This hunting query depends on HoneyForge data connector (CommonSecurityLog Parser or Table)

elements.name: huntingquery4
elements.label: HoneyForge - Repeated Probes from Same Source

options.text:
Finds source IPs that have probed HoneyForge sensors on multiple distinct
occasions separated by at least one hour, suggesting deliberate or scripted
reconnaissance rather than a one-off event.

A legitimate network scanner that hits a sensor once might be an
oversight. One that returns hours or days later is a persistent threat. This hunting query depends on HoneyForge data connector (CommonSecurityLog Parser or Table)

Identifies the source IP addresses that have interacted most frequently with
HoneyForge deception sensors over the past 7 days. Repeat offenders across
multiple sensors are especially high-priority  - they indicate persistent
reconnaissance or an automated scanner that missed the exclusion list.

Use this query as a starting point for threat-intel enrichment and to decide
which IPs warrant a block rule or further investigation. This hunting query depends on HoneyForge data connector (CommonSecurityLog Parser or Table)
